title: Air India Restores Nonstop Delhi and Mumbai to New York Flights as Iraq Airspace Reopens
excerpt: The Rome fuel stop is gone on four routes to JFK and Newark, cutting journeys from almost 20 hours to 15-16 — though January headwinds could bring stops back.
body:
• Air India has restored nonstop flights between Delhi, Mumbai and New York (JFK and Newark) since Wednesday, dropping the Rome fuel stop and cutting journey times by close to four hours.
  • Flights now take 15 to 16 hours instead of almost 20, after reduced risk ratings for Iraq, Syria and Jordan opened a shorter route; Iran and Pakistan airspace remain closed to the airline.
  • The nonstops are expected to hold through November and December, but strong January headwinds and heavy loads could bring temporary fuel stops back.
  • For travellers: if you are booked to New York in November or December, your one-stop booking may now operate nonstop — check your itinerary in the Air India app before planning around a Rome layover.

Air India has made its flights between Delhi, Mumbai and New York nonstop again, shaving close to four hours off journeys that had run as one-stops through Rome since the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The change took effect on Wednesday and covers four routes — Delhi to JFK, Delhi to Newark, Mumbai to JFK and Mumbai to Newark — The Times of India reported. Journeys that took almost 20 hours with the Rome Fiumicino stop now take 15 to 16 hours.

What Changed in the Sky

The airline's operations team tracks the geopolitical risk ratings of the airspaces on its routes. As the ratings for Iraq, Syria and Jordan reduced, a slightly shorter routing became available — long enough, combined with the aircraft's range, to skip the Rome refuelling stop. Iran remains out of bounds, and Pakistan's airspace has been closed to Indian carriers since April 2025, which is why the restoration is partial rather than a return to the old routings.

https://www.instagram.com/p/Degje__jm7X/

The detours had become the winter norm. As recently as October 21, Simple Flying reported that Air India's Mumbai flights to JFK and Newark were stopping at Rome Fiumicino to refuel and change crew, and that its Delhi-New York services were scheduled to keep the stop through the winter schedule because the airline must avoid Russian, Iranian and Pakistani airspace.

"What has changed for now is that Iraq has become available again and made the flights nonstops again."

— Pilot operating the route, to The Times of India

One constraint remains. Pilots on the route told the paper there is still a load penalty — a restriction on passengers or cargo so the aircraft can carry more fuel for the longer routing — dating from Pakistan's closure. That has not changed; only the fuel stop has gone.

How Long It Lasts

The nonstops are likely to remain through November and December. From January, very strong headwinds on the westbound sector mean that if loads are high, fuel stops may return for a time. Air India is hoping Iran's airspace opens, which would let it add more nonstops to the west; nobody knows when, or whether, Pakistan will reopen its airspace to Indian carriers.

For the diaspora, the practical effect lands immediately: the Delhi and Mumbai departures to the New York area are once again single-sector flights for the Diwali and year-end travel season, with no Rome layover to misconnect through. Travellers holding January bookings should treat the nonstop as provisional and watch for schedule notices, since the airline has flagged that the winter winds — not politics — may be what brings the stop back.
